statement.text:
Let S denote the class of nondiscrete compactly generated, topologically
simple totally disconnected locally compact groups. Two topological groups are called
locally isomorphic if they contain isomorphic open subgroups. Is the number of local
isomorphism classes of groups in S uncountable?                        P.-E. Caprace

∗                                                                  P
P19.25. Let G and H be finite groups of the same order with          g∈G φ(|g|) =
  h∈H φ(|h|), where φ is the Euler totient function. Suppose that G  is simple. Is
H necessarily simple?                                   B. Curtin, G. R. Pourgholi
  ∗ No,  it need not be (P. Monticone,      Preprint,  2026,  https://
kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/19_25.
pdf).
